articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Hickory Ridge
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in July.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings. The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Yolanda Whitcomb, who has lived in Hickory Ridge for 14 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Public works estimates the work will take about 14 weeks once it begins.
The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The plan calls for basketball court along Linden Road, with work expected to start in July.

articles.title: Cedar Hollow Primary Teams Head to Summer Tournament
articles.deck: The program begins in October and is open to all students in grade 4 and up.
body: Students will meet on Wednesday afternoons in the Hickory Ridge rec center, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Principal Denise Orchard said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
The board will review the results at the end of the summer term. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for October.

articles.title: Then & Now: Kiln Street in 1980 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height. Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.
A 1980 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Kiln Street from the corner of Vine Street.

body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
